newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen up on short-covering, rate comments.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen up on short-covering, rate comments.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures showed a firmer bias in late Friday trade as players covered their short positions ahead of U.S. jobs data at 1230 GMT.

Dealers said the market also received a slight boost from wire reports quoting the head of the Federation of Bankers Association of Japan, Naotaka Saeki, as saying he did not think the Bank of Japan was ready to raise interest rates.
But they said there had been no change in sentiment in the Japanese interest rate futures market and players would still choose to sell into any rallies.
"It looks like today was just some position adjustment ahead of the weekend. The locals were very short," a trader with a Japanese futures house said.
But he added that December Euroyen would face resistance around 98.92/93. The contract stood at 98.90 at 1115 GMT after touching a high of 98.91 against an IMM close at 98.86.
September JGBs ended at 122.92 against their previous 122.71.
Eurodollar futures were little moved as players sat on their hands ahead of the U.S. non-farm payrolls report for May.
Economists polled by Reuters expected on average that non-farm payrolls would rise by 219,000 while average hourly earnings were expected to be up by 0.4 percent.
December Eurodollars ended at 93.790 against their IMM close at 94.790. They are expected to remain in a 94.75-94.85 range if the jobs data comes in within expectations.
